title: Ide Igbo
description: The history, and the relationship between the dialect and the wider Igbo world.
html:
Ide History

Ide people are a subgroup of Igbo people founded by Idenze Ezeme (Nze) from Nkpor, in Idemmili. It was spearheaded by the 10 children of Nze, from whom the 7 clans came. The last three kids are the protectors of the first kid, Isiome, who founded the Ezeme’s Uniku.

Ide Igbo Titled Men's Clothing

(Uwe Ibobo)

Ide clothing shall be called “Uwe ibobo”, a reference to the Igbo word for “aura” which is modernly called “steeze.” Many cultural wears will inspire this clothing style.

The first design will be from Igbo clothing and will be called “Uwe ogodo. Uwe Ibobo is only for titled men.

Uwe Ogodo

This clothing design is the exact style that will be used for Uwe Ibobo. Now, it’ll be designed with Anioma clothing “Akwa Ocha” material to represent the purity reputation of the Ide king.

The chest styling pattern

The chest styling pattern of Uwe ibobo will be designed with “agu” totem, which is the Igbo leopard totem. It’ll be created with Akwaete, and it’ll be reddish too.

Lion head

The final thing that will differentiate Otu Nze and Ikala is the leopard skin that will be crossed over, but Ide’s type will have the head skin of the leopard hanging on his shoulder. Also, Uwe ibobo will be a skirt, instead of ogodo.

The dressers of the Nyimi des BaKuba (DRC)

Uwe Ibobo will be a skirt just as this picture depicts above. It’ll have the same styling as the skirt, and the round design at the edges will be designed with Akwaete. This now makes Uwe ibobo the combination of Akwa Ocha and Akwaete. It’ll be reddish like the Igbo earth's soil. It’ll also have the tail-like design, like the picture depicted.

This unique clothing will separate Ide from the rest of the Igboid group, but still represent the larger Igbo identity.

Ide King & Queen Crown & Chiefs Cap

King's Crown:

Ide kings will have a unique crown designed to be a mixture of Igbo and a few cultures. The crown will be inspired by the headdress of Kazakh brides, which is called the “saukele.”

saukele sketch

This sketch explains how the styling will be, but with Igbo symbols (including ndebe script symbols). To understand the concept more, below are images of its design in precolonial times and post-colonial times:

This particular design fits perfectly if it’s to be mixed with four eagle feathers that represent east, west, north, and south, as well as the four Igbo market days. The symbols will have Python totem, eagle totem, leopard totem, lion totem, ram totem, cow totem, tortoise totem, owl totem, and crocodile totem. This crown will also have feathers of the newly created pigeon that will be called “wulului”, which came from “wululuyn,” an Austronesian language called Bundjalung. It is their word for wonga pigeon. The feathers on the crown will be facing the sky.

Depiction of how the feathers will look

The eagle feathers on the crowns of every Ikala represent every clan under him. Then the wulului pigeon feathers will be used on the crown to convey the beauty of Ana Ide.

Queen's Crown:

Ide queens will have a unique crown that differentiates them from other Igbo queens. Ide queens are called “Iyi, which translates to stream in central Igbo. Iyi is a river in Igbo, so the queen must always come from Iyi royal families. The Queen is not married to the King because Ide practices a two-monarchy system. The queen rules along with the king.

Mongol traditional crown

This is how the crown will be designed, but the beads will have Igbo symbols and designs, with gold. To differentiate it from this one in the picture above, it has a two-python-head gown downward and is lapped over her shoulders.

Mongol queen's crown

This is how the python will lap on her, as the black and white picture of the last Mongol queen’s crown lapped on hers. But it’ll not be as big as that since it will be depicting a python. Also, the end of it will show the Python head. The python will be small and look like a real python, even though it is synthetic. It’ll be uniquely designed with beads, and it’ll also have feathers like the king’s crown. Both eagle and wulului pigeon fathers.

Chiefs Cap:

The chief's cap will be a mixture of Igbo red cap, Onicha Ado Okpu Ozo and Bhutan king’s crown.

Igbo red cap

This is how Ide red cap will be designed, so that it’ll be able to accommodate. The round head design they put on the design on will be positioned like the king of Bhutan’s crown. But then, the round fold will have the styling in Okpu Ozo, just that it’ll now have Ide Igbo symbols.

Okpu Ozo Onicha

This round design in Onicha Okpu Ozo is the type of styling that will be in Okpu-Ide, which is Ide chief's staff. The symbols won’t be the same as Okpu Ozo, but it’ll be the same styling.

Bhutan Raven King Crown

This Bhutan’s Raven Crown is how the round fold that has symbol styles will situate be, but will be as strong as Okpu Ozo. Then the older version style is how the Igbo red will bend so that it’ll have a way for the eagle head. Ide will use eagle head instead of raven. This cap will be worn by Nde Eze. Nde Nze will have a society called “Ugonze.” They can also call it “Otu Ugo.”

African fish eagle

This eagle head will replace the raven head on the Bhutanese king's crown. The Ikala will have the white-headed eagle head, while the Nde Nze gets any other colour.

Ofona Staff

Ofona is Ide traditional staff for Nde Nze Ide, which will be styled with Igbo’s oto nsi/alo and a mixture of Saka king (Kazakh), and Sarmatian leader's staff. The head of the staff will be Python, which represents the deity Idemmili, who is the river Goddess.

Ofo nsi/alo

This picture of Igbo traditional chiefs' staff called otonsi/alo is how slim it’ll be for Nde Nze, and their own middle pattern will be designed using Python. The head for Nde Nze will be the same as this, but with Python styling that represents the four cardinal directions and four market days. The one for Ikala will not have the middle pattern.

Nde Nze staff head styling

This picture depicts the way Nde Nze Ofona head styling will be. It’ll be in the same way otonsi is designed.

Saki (Kazakh) king

The way the body of this staff is shaped is how Ikala royal staff will be, but the round styling will be of python. The colour of the staff for Nde Nze will be black, while the one for Kings and Queens will be reddish to represent both blood and red earth.

Oru’iku staff head styling

This is how the head of every Iyi Ofona head will be styled.

Ikala staff head styling

The head styling for kings of Ide will be a leopard head. This distinguishes the roles the king and queen play in society.

Ide Queen’s Dress

Iyi dress will be inspired by modern Nigerian glamorous dresses with a touch of Uwe ibobo at the edges, just like the king’s dress.

The upper part will look like the one in this picture, which gives her space for air.

Mongol traditional fashion

The way the lower part of this Mongol dress was styled is the way the queen’s dress will be styled, but material of the clothing will be Akwa Ocha. These edges will have a similar design to the king’s version, and also be designed with Akwaete. And then the section with the design above the edges will also be designed with Akwaete.

Akwaete design

This round “aji” around the Akwaete design is going to be in the queen's dress to show how glamorous and fierce she is.

Akwaete

The edges after the Akwaete circle design will now have the Akwaete design, like it is in the edges of the picture above. This will enable the dress to look more traditional.

The stomach part will be designed the way this one was done with both wool and beads to create a unique styling like it is in the picture. The design will represent Python totem.

Wulului Pigeon

This will be a special pigeon that will be imported from Australia to Ide kingdom. This bird symbolises the beauty of Ide. The Pigeon will be both Common and Brush bronzewing. The first set of this pidgin will be 200 pcs. 100 of Common, and 100 of Brush. Each species will be 70% female and 30% male.

Wulului will represent the beauty of Ide kingdom.

Bronzewing Pigeon

Another bird that will populate Ana Ide is Kestrel Hovers, which will be found mostly in the planned forest areas with tall trees.

Ide Traditional Female Clothing

This clothing design will be styled with a mixture of Igbo traditional clothing styles and Zulu traditional clothing styles. Ide women will have three skirt styles for young women.

First Skirt Style:

The first design will be styled to fit Igbo women's traditional dress, but with Akwa Ocha and Akwaete.

Igbo clothing

This clothing design is very important because it is suitable for our environment and also depicts original Igbo clothing. However, the material will be Akwa Ocha, while the designs on the clothing will be Akwaete. Ide people will always use the mixture of Akwa Ocha and Akwaete. The white styling at the edges of the skirt will be of Akwaete, while the main skirt will be Akwa Ocha.

Isi agu material

This picture shows the gap that is needed for the first skirt style so that women can wear beads or something around their waist.

Second Skirt Style:

The second style will be styled like a Zulu woman's traditional skirt, but this time around, it’ll be designed with Akwa Ocha and Akwaete. This is to make the design Igbotic.

Zulu traditional style

This styling from Zulu girls will be the same as Ide styling for young women with Akwa Ocha and Akwaete as the material. Akwa Ocha will be the main skirt material, while Akwaete will be the design around the Waist. This is to make it unique from others. The design pattern will be of Akwaete symbols just like the dress depicted above.

Akwaete patterns

This is how the patterns will be on the skirt, instead of the South African pattern.

Third Skirt Style:

This third style will also be styled like Zulu black and white traditional wear with lots of beads. This style will be designed in the same way Igbo maidens' skirts are, but with the design styling of Zulu young girls' skirts. This is more like a tight skirt

Igbo maiden

This will be styled in a similar way as it is in the pictures, but the skirts will now be designed like Zulu women's tight skirts. This is to show that the design pattern can work with Akwa Ocha and Akwaete, since the pictures were done with Akwaete.

Zulu skirt

This Zulu skirt design is how the third skirt will be. It’ll be made with Akwa Ocha, as this is showing white parts, and then the non-white parts will be done with Akwaete. The Akwaete colour will most likely be blue or black. This is to fit the skirt pattern as it is in the picture.

Waist Style:

The clothing will have special ornaments for the waist to separate it from other Igbo clothing and the Zulu clothing.

Zulu beaded belt

This Zulu belt will be redesigned to be Igbotic. The lower picture shows the pattern of the waist beads, while the top shows. The top one is perfect, but it’ll not have the square in the middle. It’ll carry Uli and Akwaete patterns.

Beaded belts

This pattern in the image looks similar to the designs on Akwaete, which means Ide beaded belts will be designed with Akwaete and Uli patterns to showcase how Igbotic it is.

Igbo jigida

On top of the beaded belt, the clothing requires jigida on the same waist because jigida is the most important bead for women during ceremonies in Igbo land. This picture shows exactly how Jigida is worn by Igbo women.

Ide Traditional Male Clothing

Ide male clothing be skirt like the Kuba Nyim dressers, just like Uwe Ibobo, but this one will not have the style on the waist.

Twins tradition

When one of the twins dies, they must make a statue for the dead one. This came from Yoruba tradition.

Festival Traditions

There should be something like a Halloween tradition that happens in November, but a traditional version.

Ndenka (Craftsmen)

Among Ide Igbo people, the most highly respected artisans will be the smiths, since the smiths will be considered magicians, and their work will be shrouded in mysticism. They will be called "The First Sons of the Earth”
